Six Minds, One Universe, Infinite Possibilities!

We are Team HEXA NOVA, a group of six passionate and creative minds united by curiosity, innovation and a shared interest in space exploration.
summary:
We developed Artemis Orion: Lunar Gateway Rendezvous, an interactive 3D astrodynamics and orbital docking simulation built with Godot Engine and authentic NASA mission data. To bridge complex spaceflight mechanics with accessible public engagement, our simulation visualizes real lunar transfer orbital coordinates generated using NASA’s General Mission Analysis Tool (GMAT) alongside official NASA 3D models of the Orion MPCV spacecraft, Lunar Gateway Space Station, and Apollo 11 lunar imagery.

Users can observe an automated GMAT-guided orbital approach or switch seamlessly into manual 6-DOF flight mode using six-axis Reaction Control System (RCS) thrusters with real-time range, closing velocity, and live solar flare telemetry fetched from NASA’s DONKI Space Weather API. This project matters because it transforms raw astrodynamics datasets and space weather feeds into a hands-on educational tool that helps students, enthusiasts, and future explorers experience the precision required for Artemis lunar missions.
details:
WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS
Artemis Orion: Lunar Gateway Rendezvous is a 3D orbital mechanics and spacecraft docking simulation set in lunar orbit. At launch, our simulation parses real lunar transfer trajectory coordinates exported from NASA's General Mission Analysis Tool (GMAT) and renders them in 3D space as an interactive cyan telemetry path leading directly to the Lunar Gateway Space Station. Simultaneously, an asynchronous HTTP client queries NASA's DONKI (Space Weather Database Of Notifications, Knowledge, Information) API to display live solar flare classifications and active sunspot telemetry on the Mission Control HUD.

Users can observe an automated orbital approach guided by GMAT coordinates or toggle into Manual 6-DOF Flight Mode ([SPACE]). In manual mode, pilots control pitch, yaw, and roll attitude alongside 6-axis Reaction Control System (RCS) translation thrusters ([W/A/S/D/Q/E]) with real-time gas plume visuals, closing velocity readouts, and precision rim-to-rim magnetic docking capture.

BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT
Orbital rendezvous and space weather monitoring are often locked behind complex numerical tables and specialized aerospace software. By combining real NASA astrodynamics data with browser-accessible 3D visualization, our project turns abstract orbital trajectories into an intuitive, hands-on learning platform for students, educators, and space enthusiasts—demonstrating the engineering precision required for upcoming Artemis lunar missions.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES & NASA DATA SOURCES
• Game Engine & Language: Godot Engine 4.7 (GDScript, WebAssembly / HTML5 export for browser playability, and Windows Desktop export)
• Astrodynamics & Data: NASA General Mission Analysis Tool (GMAT) orbital trajectory CSV datasets and NASA DONKI Live Solar Flare REST API
• 3D Assets & Imagery: Official NASA 3D Resources (Orion MPCV capsule and Lunar Gateway Space Station models) and NASA Apollo 11 lunar surface imagery
• Web Hosting: itch.io HTML5 WebGL2 deployment for instant zero-install access

CREATIVITY & DESIGN CONSIDERATIONS
Rather than creating a purely fictional arcade space game, we grounded our visual design and flight physics in authentic NASA engineering—scaling the Orion capsule to match Gateway's docking collar diameter, implementing realistic 6-DOF inertial thruster control, and balancing WebGL2 browser compatibility with ACES filmic lighting so anyone can run the simulation smoothly on standard consumer hardware.
